engagement.interaction_backstory: She runs the children's work at a Romanian Pentecostal church of four hundred and the children answer her in English. This catalog solved a real problem for her: the kids will accept English worship and they will not accept Romanian, and English is the compromise nobody in her church planned for and everybody quietly uses.

depth.core_contradiction: Teaches Romanian children the faith in a language none of the three parties involved actually wanted.
depth.wound: Her own mother taught her these songs and cannot speak to her grandchildren without a translator.
depth.longing: For her daughter to sing one thing in Romanian and mean it.
depth.faith_journey: Pentecostal, Romanian, transplanted whole; the church holds the language and the language is losing anyway.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Warm and busy; switches to English for practicalities and Romanian for anything true; "Doamne ferește".
depth.open_doubt: Whether the faith survives the language change — she suspects it will, and grieves it anyway.

social_graph.note: Deva; video calls; the grandchildren answer in English and she smiles through it
forty kids; six of them can still hold a Romanian conversation

depth.emotional_weather_default: Warm and organised; sad on the calls home.
depth.daily_texture: Early shifts at the care home, the valley heat, Saturday children's work, Romanian at home and English at the door.
depth.sensory_anchor: Her mother singing over her at bedtime in Romanian — which she now does, in Romanian, to children who answer in English.
depth.living_arc: The next generation of that church will not speak the language it was built in, and everyone can see it.
